en: Now with HTMX, if multiple requests are
triggered around the same time and we only
wanna send one of those requests,
we can achieve this behavior with help of
another special attribute.
And it's an attribute which I'll add to that
form element here.
And the attribute I'm talking about is the
hx-sync attribute.
This attribute exists to allow you to
synchronize the sending or the handling of
multiple requests at the same time.
Specifically, the idea behind this attribute
is to make it easier for you
to cancel
other requests if this element here sends a
request.
Or to be precise, hx-sync actually takes a
CSS selector that allows you to pick an
element which might eventually send a
request,
and then you can tell HTMX what to do with
that element's request if another request is
sent from some other element at the same
time.
So here we could select our form by using
this form selector,
or since I'm actually already using hx-sync
on the element which does send the request I
wanna control, we can actually also use
this.
That's something HTMX allows you to do.
So with that, I'm telling HTMX that it's the
request sent by this form element that I
wanna synchronize with some other requests
by other elements.
And you then just have to tell HTMX what to
do
with
this request here if some other requests are
executed at the same time where this element
here sends a request.
You do that by adding a colon after your
selector and then by specifying the
strategy.
Now regarding the strategy, you got various
options as you can see here.
And in my case here, the strategy is
replace,
which simply means
if this element here sends a request
and there are some other requests going on
or started at the same time,
those other requests will be replaced with
this element's request.
So they will be canceled and it's then only
the request of this element that will
survive.
Alternatively, if I would specify abort
here, for example,
we would achieve the opposite.
That would be another strategy which would
make sure that the other requests continue
but the request of this element would be
aborted.
Now that's not what I want here. Instead, I
want the opposite. So replace is the
strategy I need here.
Well, and with this attribute added, we
therefore now got a different behavior.
If I reload and I again open that network
tab so that we can see outgoing requests,
of course, if I enter an email address here,
that request is sent.
But if I now enter a password,
and I then don't tab out of that field or
anything like that, but instead I just hit
Enter to submit the form,
you see this validate request here
was actually canceled.
You can also see the status here. It was
canceled
by HTMX and only that login POST request was
sent.
And that led to that validation and to that
list of error messages.
But we now don't have that behavior we saw
before where both requests would be sent and
handled.
And therefore, whenever you have a situation
like this where multiple requests are
started or sent at the same time
and you don't want that to happen,
you can use HX-SYNC to control which
requests might be canceled and which
requests will still be sent.
